export_rights.summary: Per the Sage Intacct Terms of Service (US), Customer Data may be exported at any time during the term of the Agreement. After termination or expiration, Sage will not delete Customer Data from its production environment for up to 90 days and may assist with export during that period at its standard hourly consulting rate; after the 90-day period Sage may delete all Customer Data. Paid archival services may be available for longer storage.
export_rights.post_termination_window: 90 days (data retained in production up to 90 days post-termination; vendor export assistance billed at standard hourly consulting rates)

routes.how: Data Delivery Service (DDS): subscribe via Company > Admin > Subscriptions > Data Delivery Service > Configure, define a cloud storage destination, then create export jobs per object (full export or changes-only since last export), run on demand or scheduled daily/weekly/monthly. Also drivable via API (getDdsObjects to list supported objects, run DDS jobs programmatically).
requires: Data Delivery Service subscription (separately enabled module)
a cloud storage account configured as the delivery destination
gotchas: Only certain standard objects are DDS-exportable; check the DDS Objects page or getDdsObjects for the supported list
Each object's records are delivered as separate .csv files to the cloud destination, not as a single archive
Vendor best practice is one initial full export followed by incremental changes-only jobs
The full list of supported cloud destinations was not confirmed from the docs consulted (an official developer sample uses Amazon S3)

covers: all API-readable objects (GL, AP, AR, journals, invoices, bills, customers, vendors, dimensions, etc.)
routes.how: REST API at api.intacct.com (e.g. OAuth2 endpoints https://api.intacct.com/ia/api/v1/oauth2/authorize and .../oauth2/token); OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow with Bearer tokens, apps registered in the Sage developer/app-registry portal. Sage positions REST as the recommended interface for new integrations.
requires: Sage Intacct Web Services developer license (obtained via Sage account manager)
registered app (client ID/secret) in the Sage App Registry
an Intacct company user to authorize against
routes.rate_limits: No public per-minute rate limit documented; API usage is metered as transactions under Sage's Performance Tier model (partner documentation cites 100,000 included transactions/month at the base tier, with paid overages). Third-party guides report OAuth access tokens expiring after 12 hours (43200 s).
gotchas: Web Services is a licensed add-on, not included in every contract
Rate/tier specifics above come from partner and third-party writeups, not a fetched official limits page — verify against current Sage docs

routes.how: Legacy XML Web Services API: POST XML request envelopes; two-level auth with a Web Services sender ID + password (provisioned with the developer license and authorized per company) plus a company user login or session. Use readByQuery/query per object for bulk reads, get_list on supdoc for attachments, getAuditTrail/readByQuery on AUDITHISTORY for audit records.
requires: sender ID authorized in the target company (Company > Company Info > Security web services authorizations)
company user credentials or session ID
routes.rate_limits: Metered under the same per-transaction Performance Tier model as REST (each query/readByQuery/create/update/delete call counts as one transaction). Third-party docs cite a cap of 2,000 results per readByQuery call, requiring pagination for large datasets.
gotchas: XML API is legacy: still supported but receiving no new features per Sage guidance
readByQuery result paging means large tables need many calls, which consumes the transaction allowance

covers: master records and transaction lists shown on list pages (e.g. customers, vendors, and similar per-module lists)
routes.how: From an object's list page in the UI (e.g. the Customers list under Accounts Receivable), use the list's export action to export the records; use Manage view to build a custom view controlling which fields, sort order, and records are included in the export.
gotchas: Export contents follow the current list view — fields not in the view are not exported
Per-list manual operation; there is no documented single UI action that exports every entity at once (use DDS or the API for that)

covers: custom reports (Custom Report Writer and Interactive Custom Report Writer)
audit-history custom reports (Audit History data source, full admins)
routes.how: Run a report and use 'Export as' to choose the output format. Memorized/custom reports can be scheduled (Schedule Report page, e.g. weekly/monthly) with delivery to a cloud-storage target (docs name Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, Amazon S3), an HTTP address, or storage in Intacct (My Stored Reports). Filters limit exported rows to the filtered set.
requires: report run permissions; full admin rights for a custom report on the Audit History data source
gotchas: Exporting a filtered report exports only the filtered records
Interactive Custom Report Writer is a separately licensed reporting tool

routes.how: UI: open a record's Audit Trail window and use More actions to export; company-wide, full admins can build a custom report on the Audit History data source (sortable by time, user, changed object) and export it. API: getAuditTrail on an object or readByQuery on the AUDITHISTORY object.
requires: View access to the record for per-record audit trail
full admin rights for the Audit History custom report
Web Services license for API access
gotchas: Audit capture only began May 2016; docs note inconsistencies in data captured May 2016-Feb 2017, AP/AR adjustment audit data unavailable before Nov 2016, and possible partial gaps before Oct 2019
No explicit retention/purge period is documented in the pages consulted
Advanced Audit Trail is a separate feature with its own documentation

routes.how: No bulk UI export of attachments was found in the docs consulted. Via the XML API, read the supdoc object (get_list/read): each supporting document returns its name, type, creation details, and file content as a base64-encoded string; transactions reference their attachments via SUPDOCID fields (labeled 'Attachments' in the UI).
gotchas: Attachment payloads are base64 and can be very large — developer docs advise limiting returned fields and maxitems per call
Extraction is per-document iteration; there is no documented archive/zip bulk download

routes.how: Customization Services: group customizations into a customization package — an XML document conforming to the Sage Intacct package XSD — which can be exported and re-imported into another company. Platform Services: an application (custom objects, standard-object extensions, menus) can be published as an XML file and installed on a target company; individual component definitions can be exported from the UI via 'Export Def'.
requires: Customization Services or Platform Services subscription
gotchas: Custom reports and standard configuration settings are not documented as part of these XML packages — coverage of package contents should be verified in-tenant

preservation_notes.attachments: No documented bulk UI export; pull each supdoc record via the XML API (get_list/read on supdoc), which returns file content base64-encoded with name/type metadata, iterating over SUPDOCIDs referenced by transactions.
preservation_notes.audit_log: Export per-record audit trails from the Audit Trail window (More actions > CSV/Excel/PDF), or company-wide via a full-admin custom report on the Audit History data source, or via API (getAuditTrail / readByQuery on AUDITHISTORY). Capture began May 2016 with documented gaps before Oct 2019; no explicit retention cap documented — verify in-tenant.
preservation_notes.config_artifacts: Customizations export as XML customization packages (conforming to the package XSD) and Platform Services applications publish as installable XML files; individual component definitions export via 'Export Def' in the UI. Whether custom reports and module configuration settings are captured is not documented — verify in-tenant.

notes: Research caveat: the network egress proxy blocked direct fetches of intacct.com, developer.intacct.com, and developer.sage.com, so vendor-page content was consulted through search-engine excerpts of those exact pages rather than full page fetches; nav paths and claims should be re-verified against the live docs and tenant. Honest unknowns: no single-click whole-company backup/export exists in the docs consulted — DDS is the closest whole-tenant route and is a separately subscribed module; the complete list of DDS cloud-storage destinations was not confirmed (S3 appears in an official developer sample; report scheduling separately documents Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, Amazon S3); official current API rate-limit/Performance-Tier numbers were only seen via partner/third-party sources; audit-trail retention has documented capture-start dates (May 2016) and pre-2019 gaps but no documented purge window; Advanced Audit Trail exists as a distinct feature and was not researched in depth. API access of any kind requires a paid Web Services developer license.
